title: Kaempferol attenuates microglial activation in Alzheimer's disease via inhibiting the cytosolic HK2-mediated NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Wang, Mengyao; Guo, Minsong; Li, Simeng; Song, Liyu; Wu, Meihong; Zhao, Jiahui; Xu, Tengfei; Zhou, Yuan
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究山奈酚通过抑制HK2介导的NF-kappaB信号减轻阿尔茨海默病小胶质细胞炎症，虽含分子对接但核心为药物-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Kaempferol (KAE), a natural flavonoid with substantial anti-inflammatory activity, has demonstrated efficacy against Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the fundamental mechanisms are not yet fully understood. OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to elucidate the role of KAE in alleviating microglia-mediated neuroinflammation in AD and its underlying mechanisms. METHODS: The 3 x Tg-AD mice and LPS-stimulated BV2 microglial cells were employed as in vivo and in vitro model respectively. The HK-TAT peptide was utilized to induce mitochondrial dissociation of HK2, and 3-BP was applied as a HK2 inhibitor. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses were performed to discover the inhibitory effect of KAE on HK2. Immunofluorescence and Western blotting were employed to explore the suppressive role of KAE in cytosolic HK2-mediated NF-kappaB signaling. Additionally, the interaction between KAE and HK2 was investigated through molecular docking, validated by SPR, and confirmed via CETSA. RESULTS: Our findings demonstrated that KAE significantly attenuated LPS-induced microglial activation, along with the release of pro-inflammatory factors and enhanced glycolytic activity. In vivo, KAE partially rescued cognitive impairment and neuronal damage in 3 x Tg-AD mice. Microglial activation was also markedly suppressed. Mechanistically, we revealed that dissociation of HK2 from mitochondria to the cytosol was sufficient to induce microglial activation, and this process was consequently constrained by the suppression of HK2 level and activity using 3-BP. By reducing HK2 levels, KAE suppressed cytosolic HK2-mediated IkappaBalpha phosphorylation and subsequent nuclear translocation of NF-kappaB. Furthermore, KAE not only downregulated HK2 transcription but also bound to HK2, promoting its ubiquitination-mediated degradation. CONCLUSION: Our data indicate that KAE alleviates microglia-mediated neuroinflammation in AD, which correlates with the suppression of HK2 and the modulation of cytosolic HK2-dependent NF-kappaB activation.
abstract_zh: 引言：山奈酚（Kaempferol, KAE）是一种具有显著抗炎活性的天然黄酮类化合物，已被证明对阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）有效。然而，其基本机制尚未完全阐明。目的：本研究旨在阐明KAE在缓解AD中小胶质细胞介导的神经炎症中的作用及其潜在机制。方法：采用3 x Tg-AD小鼠和LPS刺激的BV2小胶质细胞分别作为体内和体外模型。利用HK-TAT肽诱导HK2从线粒体解离，并应用3-BP作为HK2抑制剂。通过转录组学和代谢组学分析发现KAE对HK2的抑制作用。采用免疫荧光和Western blotting探讨KAE对胞质HK2介导的NF-kappaB信号通路的抑制作用。此外，通过分子对接研究KAE与HK2之间的相互作用，并经SPR验证，再通过CETSA确认。结果：我们的研究结果表明，KAE显著减弱了LPS诱导的小胶质细胞活化，以及促炎因子的释放和糖酵解活性的增强。在体内，KAE部分改善了3 x Tg-AD小鼠的认知障碍和神经元损伤。小胶质细胞活化也受到显著抑制。机制上，我们揭示HK2从线粒体解离至胞质足以诱导小胶质细胞活化，而这一过程随后通过使用3-BP抑制HK2水平和活性而受到限制。通过降低HK2水平，KAE抑制了胞质HK2介导的IkappaBalpha磷酸化及随后的NF-kappaB核转位。此外，KAE不仅下调HK2转录，还结合HK2，促进其泛素化介导的降解。结论：我们的数据表明，KAE缓解AD中小胶质细胞介导的神经炎症，这与抑制HK2及调节胞质HK2依赖性NF-kappaB激活相关。
